heading: Power laws fitted on small runs predict loss at much larger scales
definition: power laws fitted on small runs predict the loss of runs orders of magnitude larger.
summary: Several independent groups report accurate forecasts within specific setups, including 0.7% error at about 300× compute and errors within 0.66% through 113× compute. General extrapolation remains contested: some Pythia and translation fits fail, while prospective forecasts spanning multiple orders of magnitude above 100B parameters lack established validation with calibrated uncertainty.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 for setup-specific loss forecasting at <1B, 1–10B and 10–100B; C for unrestricted extrapolation across these settings. Above 100B, ? for prospective numerical multiple-order forecasting with calibrated uncertainty. Toy scale is not separately identified in versions.V2.studies_by_size.
suggested_status.reason: The unqualified version has recorded failures as well as independent setup-specific successes. arXiv:2403.08540#R5/#R6 reports 0.7% error at about 300× compute; arXiv:2607.23377#R2–#R6 reports errors within 0.66% through 113× compute. arXiv:2410.11840#R7 reports non-predictive smallest-Pythia fits, and arXiv:2409.15051#v2-fit-410/#v2-fit-1b reports failed translation extrapolation. counts versions.V2.studies_with_challenges=10 and versions.V2.studies_with_limits_scope=66 document qualifications; versions.V2.studies_by_size includes >100B but does not establish prospective validation. versions.V2.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original=2 distinguishes limited author overlap from the broader evidence pool.
suggested_status.open_questions: Prospective forecasts with frozen fitting procedures, numerical residuals and calibrated uncertainty across multiple-order gaps; matched comparisons isolating minimum fitting scale, target-regime coverage, functional form and optimization; comparable validation above 100B and in instruct/chat settings.

source.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
source.authors: Jared Kaplan; Sam McCandlish; Tom Henighan; Tom B. Brown; Benjamin Chess; Rewon Child; Scott Gray; Alec Radford; Jeffrey Wu; Dario Amodei

original_result.setup: The original study fitted Transformer language-model loss against parameter count and training steps after the initial transient, using an infinite-data approximation.
original_result.result: The training-curve fit used exponents of 0.077 for parameter count and 0.76 for training steps. This fit alone does not establish prediction accuracy orders of magnitude beyond the fitted runs.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Prospective numerical loss forecasts with calibrated uncertainty for text models above 100B parameters across multiple-order fit-to-target gaps.
untested.basis: counts versions.V2.studies_by_size includes >100B, so absence of that size is not claimed. arXiv:2005.14165#R1 is a plotted continuation without a new numerical forecast; arXiv:2410.11840#R6 is retrospective within-family estimation, and #R3–#R5 concern borrowed coefficients. The records do not establish prospective uncertainty calibration.

untested.what: Loss extrapolation explicitly categorized as instruct/chat.
untested.basis: counts versions.V2.studies_by_stage and versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.scaling.by_stage have no instruct/chat category. Fine-tuning, reasoning and preference/RL coverage does not establish this separate category.

untested.what: Controlled cross-family tests separating full small-run refitting from transfer of published exponents or partially fixed coefficients.
untested.basis: counts versions.V2.studies_by_family records family coverage, not matched transfer protocols. arXiv:2511.08066#r1 transplants Kaplan's exponent; arXiv:2410.11840#R3–#R5 borrow coefficients. Other within-family successes do not supply the missing controlled comparison.

untested.what: Numerical residuals and matched BF16 validation for Capybara's approximately 100× low-precision LLaMA extrapolation.
untested.basis: arXiv:2501.02423 untested-parts line and #r5–#r7 state visual low-precision validation without numerical errors or BF16 extrapolation. counts versions.V2.studies_by_family and versions.V2.studies_by_size establish broad coverage but do not encode precision-matched validation.

untested.what: Multiple-order extrapolation of fine-tuning loss, long-context CPT loss or agentic-RL loss-equivalent outcomes.
untested.basis: counts versions.V2.studies_by_stage and versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.evaluation.by_stage show relevant stage coverage, not extrapolation distance. The untested-parts lines and arXiv:2502.06042#r4, arXiv:2610.29352#R4/#R11 and arXiv:2610.23946#r43 restrict checks to short parameter, token or compute extensions.

untested.what: Observed loss validation of synthetic-data forecasts at 8T tokens or 400B parameters, and of the much larger looped-MoE forecasts.
untested.basis: arXiv:2510.01631#R3/#R4 are explicitly unobserved forecasts. arXiv:2609.40316's untested-parts line states that its 1.5×10^22-FLOP trillion-token runs have no observed-versus-predicted loss. counts versions.V2.studies_by_size and versions.V2.rows_by_state do not identify validation of these particular targets.

wording_issues.issue: Accurate local forecasts often cover much shorter gaps: Cerebras about 3.7× compute; DiLoCo about 4× parameters; synthetic-data validation 2× tokens and 1.5× parameters; Armenian validation only 30% larger. These results establish local extrapolation.

The extrapolation axis varies: fixed-size GPT2 extends training horizon; protein scaling increases parameters at fixed tokens; DeepSeek extrapolates compute; MusicPile also extrapolates mixture fraction. An unspecified size gap conflates these settings.

Successful predictors can require shape augmentation, schedule-aware terms, multilingual transfer/repetition terms or music-specific interactions and overfitting terms. Their success does not establish equivalent extrapolation by an unmodified power law.

Some evidence uses a prior published curve, a transferred exponent, cross-validation with interpolation mixed in, or testing points whose upward extrapolation status is unspecified. These protocols do not uniformly constitute fitting small runs and predicting larger ones.

Large-target agreement is sometimes qualitative or figure-only, without numerical residuals: DeepSeek, large loss trajectories, protein scaling and Capybara. The trajectory result also has a warm-up exception.
Targets include training loss, benchmark-derived loss, negative ELBO and log(LongPPL). These measurements cannot silently substitute for absolute held-out text pretraining loss.

Ranking, matched slopes, between-model gaps and threshold crossings do not establish absolute-loss prediction over orders of magnitude. View synthesis evaluates model-choice ranking; world modeling selects a comparison point by matching loss; Qwen-2.5 width pruning fits on 0.5B and 1.5B parameters and predicts 3B with R² 0.8627; mixed-modal scaling reports a competition-barrier crossing without a numerical absolute-loss prediction error. The pruning test leaves V2's orders-of-magnitude gap untested.

The statement supplies no accuracy tolerance or setup qualification. Results range from sub-percent errors to non-predictive smallest-Pythia fits and Figure 9(a) R² −2.1259 when over-training fitting data are omitted. That R² is not separately reported for held-out points; the study explicitly reports deteriorating prediction of over-trained models.

Forecast curves without corresponding observed runs are not validation. Synthetic-data targets at 8T tokens and 400B parameters remain forecasts; CAMEL's larger target is evaluated through benchmark performance of chosen mixtures. Continuous-speech testing points have unspecified extrapolation status.

method_sensitivity.what: Sparse L-shape sampling increases Chinchilla far-target errors: full-grid versus L-shape far MAPE is 2.46±0.19% versus 9.82±0.48% on Farseer, and 5.17±0.28% versus 14.63±0.39% on SK-Grid. Results also change with cheap versus full fitting pools and with Iso-Parameter versus localized CARBS acquisition. These are observed method sensitivities; V2 extrapolation results are mixed. The acquisition study's local LLM discussion favors Kaplan under CARBS, while its later Figure 14 discussion claims consistent Chinchilla3 superiority.

method_sensitivity.factor: Minimum fitting scale, checkpoints and onset regime
method_sensitivity.what: For examples including OPT and Pythia, including early training gives ARE above 15%; excluding the first 10B tokens gives a jointly reported 4–10% range. Intermediate checkpoints generally improve prediction over end-only fits, with Figure 4 excluding approximately the first 10% of checkpoints. Raising OLMo3's fitting cutoff from 30M to 60M reduces held-out log-loss RMSE from 0.079 to 0.049. Translation extrapolation changes with included sizes and law form: Section 4.1 reports worse 6.9B approximation from smaller subsets, while Figure 3's caption reports agreement for a differently listed subset. Small-data HEP fits can return biased exponents despite apparently power-law curves; bias magnitude and larger-run prediction error are unquantified.

OpenLM tuned fits extrapolate better than untuned fits, but the explicit validation is approximately 3.1× beyond the fitting grid and does not determine V2's orders-of-magnitude claim. The 33B trajectory forecast is less accurate before about 200,000 steps; agreement is observed after that point. Accurate trajectory prediction requires an optimal learning rate, without establishing that the displayed run used a nonoptimal rate. nanoLM off-basin proxies break numerical generalization. Qwen3-MoE token forecasts change with learning rate and convergence state; these are short-horizon forecasts rather than tests of multi-order extrapolation.

Excluding over-training fitting points produces Figure 9(a) R² −2.1259 and MSE 0.9825; these statistics are not separately reported for held-out points. MuPT ordinary-law prediction is poor, while interaction-aware and SMS fits improve prediction using modified formulas over about 2–4× beyond the largest fitting model. Coupled Skaling improves prediction relative to Chinchilla from a fitting grid through 983.1M to a 1.713B target. Farseer's stretched-exponential model-size form gives average relative error 0.50%, versus Chinchilla's 2.68%. The modified-form and modest-distance successes are auxiliary fit-sensitivity evidence; they do not establish V2's power-law prediction across orders of magnitude.

method_sensitivity.factor: Repetition and proximity to the optimum
method_sensitivity.what: Small finite unique pools hide scale-dependent validation-loss penalties. A surface fitted through 511M predicts held-out 1B/2B endpoints within 0.016 bpb at low reuse and 0.057 bpb at high reuse; this limited extension leaves V2 untested. Repetition-count prediction can work near the loss minimum but fail across the grid: at 200M, PubMed/Caselaw relative-loss RMSE is 0.021/0.019 nat locally, including refined-grid counts, versus 0.560/0.641 nat over the original grid. This selector does not predict unseen-size loss offsets. Its target pool and mixture fraction are fixed; repetition jointly changes exposure and schedule length. Conventional compute-law extrapolation also fails under repetition.

method_sensitivity.factor: Evaluation domain, language and training-setup transfer
method_sensitivity.what: C4/German predictions can remain accurate where programming-language and Penn Tree Bank errors become high at large token multipliers and model sizes. OLMo forecasts differ across evaluation domains. CortexMAE data extrapolation follows its fit on HCP-YA over about 4× beyond the largest fitted split, leaving V2's orders-of-magnitude requirement untested; out-of-distribution NSD improves more slowly than predicted. ChemFM larger-run losses deviate when transferring a small-model fit across token budgets and schedules. These domain-dependent errors and departures are distinct from establishing successful multi-order extrapolation.

DeepSeek's predictions change with compute representation: 6N1D systematically overestimates large-model performance, while 6N2D underestimates it; C=MD is the alternative representation. For OPT, the protocol fixes A and α to borrowed Muennighoff et al. values and estimates remaining parameters within the target family: ARE is 37% for 8.7B→175B, 25% for 13B→175B, and 15% for 30B→175B. The last gap is below one order of magnitude. Qwen2.5 predictions import Kaplan's exponent rather than fitting it on small target-setup runs, so their errors do not test V2's specified fitting protocol. Prediction errors alone do not establish exponent or allocation dependence.

method_sensitivity.factor: Fitting objective, optimizer and parameter sharing
method_sensitivity.what: Dominated-pair fitting worsens Skaling L-shape far MAPE from 1.57±0.62% to 5.87±1.79% on Farseer and from 1.16±0.53% to 2.99±2.05% on SK-Grid. Chinchilla's Pythia 1024× holdout Huber error changes from 9.0 to 10.6 when L-BFGS/Huber fitting changes to TRF/MSE; optimizer and objective both change. Adding batch-variation fitting data gives 11.8 versus 9.0, in units of 10⁻⁵. Shared-parameter laws improve extrapolation error by more than 2× for fits below 1B predicting 1.5B. Farseer predicts code validation losses more accurately than Chinchilla at approximately 2.19× the largest fitted compute. The shared-law and code comparisons leave V2's multi-order requirement untested.

method_sensitivity.factor: Precision representation, pruning and training ratio
method_sensitivity.what: Integer-fit predictions show an upward offset when transferred to floating-point runs; discrepancy is more apparent at 4-bit precision within the tested FP4–FP32 range. Mixed-precision prediction changes with endpoint representation. Qwen-2.5 width pruning, fitted on 0.5B and 1.5B and predicting 3B, gives R² 0.8627; negative model-size-generalization R² belongs to depth pruning: Llama −0.5441 and Qwen −0.8786. Looped-transformer prediction worsens outside the fitted tokens-per-parameter range, but its budget-holdout errors pool shorter and longer budgets. These precision, pruning and ratio comparisons provide limited-range sensitivity evidence; they do not establish V2's orders-of-magnitude upward extrapolation.

Constant-Last4 long-context observations more closely match linear-decay observations than raw constant-rate checkpoints; low MAPE in log(LongPPL) can coexist with weaker trajectory R². ARM loss is 2.2468 versus 2.2231 predicted. ARM/E2D2 gaps remain close to prediction despite shared absolute-loss misses: b=16 gives 261.6 m-nats measured versus 257 predicted; b=32 gives 296.8 versus 294. These gap-only measures are auxiliary and cannot determine V2. AI-addition method rankings differ between paired-change and absolute-loss errors, but measured extrapolation is only 1.8× and 3.6× beyond the largest fitted model; the paired-change comparisons leave V2's multi-order absolute-loss prediction untested.
